title: Just launched the Steam page for my cozy train game. How would you plan wishlists before the demo?
author: Only-Self8197
selftext:
Hi all, I'm Nelson from desgood, a tiny studio. Today we put the Steam page live for **Boo! Boo! Train!**, a cozy train journey: you drive a little train through a valley that runs on a real clock (one real hour = one day, seasons change weekly), pick a line at every junction, and stop for the view. Nothing to build, nothing to fail.

**Is all build by opus 5.5 & gpt 6 astra, for every single asset included music/sfx/model**

Trailer: [youtu.be/cyjdfRaVPtU](https://youtu.be/cyjdfRaVPtU)  
Steam: [store.steampowered.com/app](https://store.steampowered.com/app/5586990/Boo_Boo_Train/?utm_source=reddit&utm_medium=community&utm_campaign=trailer_launch_2026&utm_content=aigamedev)

Where we are: page live today (0 wishlists so far), trailer out on YouTube / X / Threads, pitches going to press, and a free public demo on 1 December.

I'd love advice from people who have been through this:

1. Between page launch and the demo (about 2 weeks), what moved wishlists most for you?
2. Should we save the demo for Steam Next Fest, or release it on 1 Dec and join Next Fest later anyway?
3. For a cozy, no-fail game, which channels worked better: Reddit, TikTok/Shorts, creators, or showcases?
4. Any honest experience with how players or Steam react to AI disclosure on the store page?

Happy to share our numbers back in a few weeks if it helps anyone. Thanks!

comments.author: DrinkingAtQuarks
comments.body: Before worrying about wishlists and what people think of the AI disclosure on Steam, you should probably be thinking about why the wheels on the train spin backward and why the sheep are inside out
